priorStories.headline: Fed raises rates by quarter point
priorStories.body:
The Federal Open Market Committee unanimously increased its target for the federal funds rate to 3.75%-4%. The quarter-point increase and related implementation measures take effect September 17.

The committee said inflation remained elevated even as economic growth stayed solid.

priorStories.headline: France estimates nearly 8,000 heatwave excess deaths
priorStories.body:
France’s national health agency estimated at least 817 excess deaths during exceptionally hot weather from July 27 through August 20. That brought recorded excess mortality since June and the start of successive heatwaves to nearly 8,000.

Most of the excess deaths were among people 75 and older. The estimates cover deaths from all causes and are based on death certificates, rather than counting only deaths directly attributed to heat.

priorStories.headline: Sudan mine collapse death toll reaches 82
priorStories.body:
Rescuers had recovered 82 bodies from collapsed, interconnected shafts at the informal al-Zara gold mine in West Kordofan, local officials and activists said. Dozens of people remained unaccounted for.

Accounts differed on whether the collapse began Sunday or Tuesday evening. Limited equipment was hampering rescue work.

priorStories.headline: Syria nullifies Assad-era terrorism court rulings
priorStories.body:
Syria’s parliament voted to abolish the Counter-Terrorism Court created under Bashar Assad and nullify the legal effects of its rulings, state television reported. The vote formalized steps already taken by the country’s post-Assad authorities.

The court, established in 2012, prosecuted thousands of Syrians. United Nations bodies had criticized its lack of judicial safeguards and links to arbitrary detention and torture.

priorStories.headline: Kosovo tribunal sentences Thaci to 25 years
priorStories.body:
The EU-backed Kosovo Specialist Chambers sentenced former Kosovo President Hashim Thaci to 25 years in prison after convicting him of war crimes from the 1998-99 conflict.

The court found him guilty of crimes including murder, torture, cruel treatment and arbitrary or illegal detention. Thaci denied the charges, and either side may appeal.

candidates.summary: Russian missiles and nearly 160 drones struck Kyiv and other Ukrainian cities overnight, Ukrainian officials said. At least 18 people, including two children, were wounded in Kyiv; six were wounded in Odesa and three in Zaporizhzhia. Ukraine reported damage across eight regions, including energy infrastructure in Sumy and Odesa. Russia said it targeted vessels used by Ukraine’s military.
candidates.title: Russian overnight strikes wound civilians across Ukraine

candidates.summary: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen proposed an EU ban on social media access for children under 13 and restrictions for those ages 13 to 15. She also proposed obligations for social media platforms, video-sharing services, online games and AI chatbots serving users under 18. The measures remain proposals rather than rules in force.
candidates.title: European Commission proposes youth social media restrictions

candidates.summary: A United Nations fact-finding mission said it had reasonable grounds to believe two U.S. strikes on a school and sports facility in Iran in February were indiscriminate attacks amounting to war crimes. The mission also found that Iranian authorities committed crimes against humanity during a crackdown on anti-government protests. The U.S. and Iranian missions in Geneva did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
candidates.title: UN mission issues findings on US strikes and Iran crackdown

candidates.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy appointed Anton Kovalskyi as acting prosecutor general, according to a presidential decree published Thursday. Kovalskyi had led the Khmelnytskyi regional prosecutor’s office since July 2025. He replaces Ruslan Kravchenko, whose removal lawmakers approved Tuesday after Kravchenko resigned amid an anti-corruption investigation involving his office; Kravchenko denied involvement and has not been charged.
candidates.title: Zelenskiy appoints acting prosecutor general

candidates.summary: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi retained key economic and security ministers in her first cabinet reshuffle, including Economy Minister Minoru Kiuchi, Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama, Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi and Defence Minister Shinjiro Koizumi. Eight of 18 ministers remained in their posts. Hiroshi Nakatsuka of the Japan Innovation Party joined the cabinet as deregulation minister.
candidates.title: Japan retains key ministers in cabinet reshuffle

candidates.summary: Australia announced plans to generally bar international students from bringing partners and children, restrict student-visa renewals to people advancing to higher qualifications and introduce a ballot for backpackers seeking working-holiday visa extensions. Visitor visas would include a provision preventing holders from remaining while applying for another visa category. The government also plans to add 100 immigration-compliance officers.
candidates.title: Australia announces tighter student and working-holiday visa rules

candidates.summary: North Korean Vice Defence Minister Kim Kang Il told the Beijing Xiangshan Forum that Pyongyang would continue expanding its nuclear forces, describing the country’s nuclear-weapons status as irreversible. Separately, Kim Yo Jong rejected renewed international calls for denuclearization in a statement carried by state media. North Korean officials attributed their position to military cooperation among the United States, South Korea and Japan.
candidates.title: North Korean officials reject denuclearization and pledge nuclear expansion
